canonicalization.digest_target: the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 canonicalized protocol.json document
canonicalization.self_reference_rule: canonical_contract_sha256 is batch metadata and is not stored inside protocol.json
canonicalization.verification_rule: servers and clients MUST reject a batch when the received digest differs from the allowlisted canonical digest

supported_protocol_versions.name: legacy-tree-projection
supported_protocol_versions.description: Folder existence may be projected from name-based tree_order and live document paths. Folder identity is not authoritative.

supported_protocol_versions.name: authoritative-folders
supported_protocol_versions.description: folders is authoritative for folder existence and identity; name-based tree_order is ordering-only.

supported_protocol_versions.name: id-tree-atomic-structure
supported_protocol_versions.description: Folder and document IDs are authoritative and tree ordering references IDs. Structural writes use a server-validated atomic structure boundary when available.

folders_authoritative.meaning: The client creates, renames, moves, restores, and tombstones folders through stable folder_id rows.

tree_order_ids.meaning: tree_order child entries reference folder_id or document_id instead of names.

tombstones.meaning: The client preserves deletion identity and revision instead of inferring deletion from absence.

legacy_tree_folder_projection.meaning: The client can reconstruct non-authoritative folders from name-based tree_order for LEGACY projects only.

immutable_batch_contract_metadata.meaning: Every operation references immutable, server-verifiable contract metadata stored on its batch.

operation_attempt_history.meaning: Attempt outcomes are appended without erasing the last failure when the operation later succeeds.

atomic_structure_commit.meaning: The server can validate and commit a structure batch transactionally, including folders, document paths, tombstones, and tree ordering.

contract_allowlist_validation.meaning: The server maps canonical contract digests to permitted protocol versions and capabilities.

project_mode_migration_lock.meaning: The server serializes migration epochs and rejects concurrent or stale migration writers.

folder_tombstones.meaning: The server retains folder_id, parent_folder_id, revision, and deletion state.

id_tree_validation.meaning: The server rejects tree references to missing, deleted, cross-project, or duplicate entities.

server_rules: An operation MUST reference exactly one existing batch.
The authenticated writer and writer_device_id MUST be bound to the batch when it is created.
The server MUST reject later mutation of contract metadata.
Retries MUST reuse the same batch_id and operation_id.

rules: Current state MUST be derivable from immutable intent and append-only attempts.
Successful completion MUST NOT delete prior attempt errors.
blocked and conflict states MUST expose the blocking operation_id or stable error code when one exists.

migration_validation: Every live folder has a unique folder_id in the project.
Every live document has a unique document_id in the project.
Every parent_folder_id resolves to a live folder in the same project or is null.
Every tombstone retains entity identity and a monotonic revision.
Every ID-based tree reference resolves exactly once.
No live siblings share the same normalized storage name.

structure_write_matrix.server_behavior: Accept legacy name projection and normalize it into the current LEGACY representation.
Accept stable IDs while the project remains readable by legacy clients; do not claim ID_BASED invariants yet.
Accept only when the request carries the active migration_epoch and lock ownership permits it.
Validate against the target ID-based representation under the migration lock.
Reject structural writes with CAPABILITY_MISMATCH because ID tree references are required.
Validate and atomically apply the structure intent or reject the complete structure transaction.

server_invariants.rule: Revisions are positive and strictly increase per entity after create.
operation_id is globally idempotent: an identical replay returns the original result and a different payload is OPERATION_ID_REUSED.
A live relative path is owned by at most one document_id within a project.
In authoritative folder modes, folder existence and identity come only from folders, never from tree_order.
In ID_BASED, tree_order controls order only and every reference resolves to a live entity in the same project.
Deletion is represented by a tombstone; absence alone is not deletion.
A project sync mode never automatically moves backward.
A structure transaction is all-or-nothing at its declared atomic boundary.
Batch contract metadata is immutable and every operation remains traceable to its writer and canonical contract digest.
Folder parent relationships remain within one project and contain no cycle.

validation_order: Resolve canonical_contract_sha256 in the server allowlist.
Verify contract_version and sync_protocol_version match that entry.
Verify declared capabilities are a subset of the allowlisted capabilities for the client build.
Verify project_sync_mode and minimum_write_protocol permit the requested intent.
Validate entity revisions and server invariants.
Apply or reject the complete atomic boundary.

conditions: The document_id already exists and is live.
The relative path and parent folder assignment are unchanged.
The request does not create, rename, move, restore, delete, or reorder any entity.
Normal revision, operation_id, content hash, authorization, and edit lease checks pass.
